newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Westa plans Prochnik share sale.
newsitem.headline: Polish Westa plans Prochnik share sale.

text.p: The receiver of bankrupt Polish insurer Westa SA wants to sell its 15.4-percent-stake in garment maker Prochnik SA in the public tender offer called by National Investment Fund (NFI) No.12, the receiver said.
"I would like to sell the remaining Prochnik shares we have to NFI Piast (12)," Dorota Brzezinska-Grabarczyk told Reuters on Wednesday.
Currently the Westa receiver has 230,882 Prochnik shares after its early-February sale to NFI 12 of 149,999 shares, or 9.9 percent of the garment maker.
On Tuesday NFI 12 announced a public tender offer to buy 343,501 Prochnik shares at 11 zlotys each to up its stake to 32.9 percent.
NFI 12 is one of the 15 NFIs in Poland's mass privatisation scheme in which the funds hold stakes in and manage about 500 companies.
